description: A terminal window manager that knows what your agents are doing. Tiling panes, workspaces, sessions that survive restarts, and one Inbox for every coding agent.
vibe: Ship a terminal OS that survives restarts, and don't melt the maintainer's machine while testing it.
highlights: The skill document is embedded in the binary and its commands are tested against the command tree, so printed docs can never drift from the build.
Test runs are explicitly capped with nice and taskset to half the cores because the maintainer works on the same box; GOMAXPROCS and -p are rejected as insufficient.
The ghostty backend is a first-class build target with its own test invocation, acknowledging that a plain go test can pass while the shipped backend is broken.
Go libraries live in the same repo as nested modules with go.work, but replace directives are banned so go install @vX still resolves correctly.
The web terminal is split into a separate binary for security isolation rather than folded into the main process.
assessment: This file reflects a maintainer who has been burned by the gap between what CI proves and what users actually run, and has closed it with embedded, test-verified docs and a dedicated backend test path. The resource-capping instructions show unusual empathy for the developer's own machine, treating the test suite as a guest rather than an entitled process. The module and pinning rules are the kind of hard-won detail that prevents subtle release breakage, and they are stated as rules rather than suggestions.
